title: Classical Weyl dimension formula for split rational Lie modules
statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over $\mathbf Q$ [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra]. Suppose $\mathfrak h\subseteq\mathfrak g$ is a maximal abelian subalgebra such that the adjoint action of $\mathfrak h$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbf Q$; this is a splitting Cartan subalgebra. Let $\Phi\subset\mathfrak h^\vee$ be its nonzero adjoint weights and choose positive roots $\Phi^+$ and simple roots $\Delta$, so every root is an integer combination of the simple roots with all coefficients nonnegative or all nonpositive. For $\alpha\in\Phi$, let $h_\alpha\in[\mathfrak g_\alpha,\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}]\subseteq\mathfrak h$ be the coroot normalized by $\alpha(h_\alpha)=2$, and write $\langle\mu,\alpha^\vee\rangle=\mu(h_\alpha)$. Put $P=\{\mu\in\mathfrak h^\vee:\mu(h_\alpha)\in\mathbf Z\text{ for all }\alpha\in\Phi\}$ and $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$. Let $\lambda\in P$ satisfy $\lambda(h_\delta)\ge0$ for every $\delta\in\Delta$. Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional simple rational Lie representation of $\mathfrak g$, with a nonzero vector $v$ satisfying $hv=\lambda(h)v$ for every $h\in\mathfrak h$ and $\mathfrak g_\alpha v=0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$. Here a Lie representation and simplicity mean exactly the linear action and invariant-subspace conditions of [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Then every $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ for $\alpha\in\Phi^+$ is a positive integer and
$$\dim_{\mathbf Q}L=\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\frac{\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle}{\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle}.$$
The equality is in $\mathbf Q$ with the ordinary integer dimension on the left. It is valid over $\mathbf Q$ itself, including reducible root systems. For the zero Lie algebra the only possible weight is $0$ and the empty product and the dimension are both $1$.

source.place: Theorem 22.52, printed p.480, restricted to characteristic zero as required by the appended errata, Chapter 22, entry for p.480; its dimension specialization at the identity. Theorems 22.53 and 23.70, printed pp.481 and 507--508, supply the split characteristic-zero Lie/group formulation. Agent-formulated Lie-module dimension consequence; this statement makes no positive-characteristic assertion and uses no positive-characteristic Kempf vanishing.

proof.text: If $\mathfrak g=0$, then $\mathfrak h=0$ and $\lambda=0$. Every subspace of $L$ is invariant, so the span of any nonzero vector must be $L$ by simplicity. Thus $\dim_{\mathbf Q}L=1$, and the empty product is $1$. For the rest use the specified splitting Cartan and integrate the given action by [lem-sfb-split-charzero-lie-group-integration]. This gives a split simply connected semisimple $G$ over $\mathbf Q$ acting on the same $L$, with $X^*(T)=P$ by differentiation, the given roots and coroot pairings, and a finite spanning reduced crystallographic root datum on its character and cocharacter lattices. Its ordinary Lie weight spaces are exactly its $T$-weight spaces.

source.place: 23.70(a)--(e), pp.507--508; zero-algebra case directly from simplicity.

proof.text: Any $G$-invariant subspace is invariant for the differentiated $\mathfrak g$-action, so simplicity of $L$ makes the integrated representation simple. The weight-space identification carries the specified $v$ to a $T$-weight vector of character $\lambda$, and, since $j$ carries each $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ onto the $T$-weight space of $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ of the corresponding root, the positive-root Lie spaces of $G$ still kill it. Dominance and every pairing are unchanged. Apply [lem-sfb-split-charzero-weyl-character-identity] to get $\rho\in P$ and the actual group-algebra identity $qA(\rho)=A(\lambda+\rho)$, where $q=\sum_\mu(\dim_{\mathbf Q}L_\mu)e^\mu$. By its direct sum decomposition, $\epsilon(q)=\sum_\mu\dim L_\mu=\dim L$. This verifies the highest-weight convention through the differentiated positive-root spaces, rather than identifying opposite Borel conventions.

Apply [lem-sfb-weyl-alternant-augmentation] to this root datum. To instantiate its positivity clause without presupposing regularity of $\rho$, first choose a regular integral $\sigma_0\in P$: in an integral basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ put $\sigma_0=\sum_i t^{i-1}u_i$. Each nonzero coroot evaluates this expression to a nonzero rational polynomial in $t$. Finitely many nonzero polynomials exclude only finitely many integer values, so choose an integer $t$ outside their roots. Take $\sigma=\nu=\sigma_0$ and $q=1$ in the cited lemma; its identity is tautological. Its moreover clause gives $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbf Z_{>0}$ for every positive root. Hence $\rho$ pairs nontrivially with every root coroot (negative coroots are negatives). Apply the same lemma now with $\sigma=\rho$, $\nu=\lambda+\rho$ and the character $q$ of the preceding step. The required identity was proved there, so it gives $\dim L=\epsilon(q)=\prod_{\alpha>0}\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle/\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ in $\mathbf Q$. No step changes the ground field or assumes irreducibility of the root system.
